source.product: No real product. An invented warm-Japandi upholstered platform bed in oatmeal linen with a tall soft padded headboard, dressed with a rumpled linen duvet and two pillows, backing a synthetic stub listing.
source.generation: Four-view turnaround reference sheet generated with the codex-image skill (front, three-quarter-front-left, side profile, rear on an opaque white seamless background), cut at detected gutter boundaries by scripts/turnaround_crop.mjs, then Higgsfield multi_image_to_3d (Meshy) with should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=28000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation off, plus a linen/oak texture_prompt.
source.postProcessing: gltf-transform resize to 1024 x 1024 textures (resize only: textures were NOT re-encoded to a lossy codec and geometry was NOT simplified, so every vertex is the generator's own; 10.32 MB to 3.29 MB), then scripts/fit_glb.py 170 215 110.
source.dimensionsVerifiedAt: Not a retail product, so there is nothing external to verify against. The declared dimensions are what the mesh measures: 180.5185 x 204.4815 x 110.0 cm (w x d x h).
source.priceVerifiedAt: None. price_cents on the stub listing is invented demo data, not a real price.

knownLimitations: Generic visual proxy, not a real SKU. It may only back a synthetic stub listing.

LIST IT AT THE MEASURED NUMBERS ABOVE, NOT THE 170 x 215 x 110 BRIEF. fit_glb.py exited 1: it hit the 10 percent anisotropy cap without reaching the target box, with residuals of +10.52 cm width and -10.52 cm depth. Height is exact at 110.0 cm. As shipped this is a 180.5 cm wide, 204.5 cm deep bed, not a 170 x 215 one, so it reads as slightly wide and slightly short for a queen.

Depth is the weak axis in image-to-3D and it was weak here too: the raw mesh came back 184.4 x 189.9 x 110.1 cm, close to square in plan where the brief wants a 0.79 width-to-depth ratio. Reaching 170 x 215 would have needed about 23 percent anisotropy.
fit_glb.py applied a per-axis scale at the full 10 percent anisotropy cap, so the mesh is stretched relative to what the generator produced.

Orientation was checked against the file and is correct for this repo: the long axis is on Z and the headboard mass sits at negative Z (normalised centroid Z of -0.89 over the top 15 percent of the model's height), so the foot of the bed faces +Z. No rotation was applied.
Single merged mesh: frame, headboard, mattress, duvet and pillows are not separately addressable.
The duvet folds and pillows are reconstructed from four still views, so the bedding geometry is an approximation of the reference sheet rather than simulated cloth.
The underside and the area behind the headboard are generated, not observed. Expect approximate geometry there.
Visual quality has NOT been verified in a render. Only measurements, orientation, triangle count and byte size were checked against the file.
